classification.difficultyReason: Requires linking applet tangent gradients to table entries, plotting those entries as a new function, and recognising linear and quadratic relationships to infer equations. The tables, axes and ordered instructions scaffold these routine representation changes; recognising the cubic's quadratic gradient pattern is the hardest demand.

content.prompt:
We will continue this investigation using Desmos.

Gradient of Tangent Calculator: https://www.desmos.com/calculator/bae2ab60nl

inlines.text: , this Desmos applet will calculate the gradient of the tangent, called the derivative, at a given point.
Complete the table of values. You may need to zoom in.
Read the tangent gradient at each listed x-value in the applet.

spec.description: Blank Cartesian axes with arrows at both ends, labelled ticks every 2, and no grid.
spec.mathematics: Both axes have ticks -10 to 10 in steps of 2; zero is unlabelled. Horizontal axis x; vertical axis y=f'(x).
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent student plotting scaffold; no plotted answer.

answer.short: $f'(x)=2x$; a straight line through the origin.
answer.worked: Plot the table pairs, including $(-5,-10)$, $(0,0)$ and $(5,10)$, and join them with a straight line. Its gradient is $\frac{10-0}{5-0}=2$ and its vertical intercept is $0$, so $f'(x)=2x$.

spec.description: Complete copy of the supplied axes with the derivative line.

sizing.exceptionReason: Both labelled axes retain all negative and positive ticks. children.label: c
children.prompt: Repeat for $y=x^3$. Use the left menu of the Desmos app to change the equation.

inlines.text: Read the tangent gradient at each listed x-value in the applet.

spec.description: Blank derivative axes with arrows at both ends and no grid; unequal axis units are intentional.
spec.mathematics: Horizontal ticks -5 to 5 in steps of 1; vertical ticks -48 to 48 in steps of 8; zero unlabelled.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent student plotting scaffold; no plotted answer.

answer.worked: Plot the table pairs and join them with a smooth curve. The graph is symmetric about the vertical axis and passes through $(0,0)$, $(\pm1,3)$, $(\pm2,12)$, $(\pm3,27)$ and $(\pm4,48)$. Each gradient is three times the square of its $x$-value, so $f'(x)=3x^2$.
